# Recorded Claude output

Each file is Claude Code 2.1.332's stdout, recorded live on haiku with `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config` in a throwaway git repo, with `{"model":"haiku"}` in `.claude/settings.local.json`. The working folder is replaced with `/tmp/rec`. The `account`, `pid` and `user_output_styles_dir` of the initialize reply and the `memory_paths` and `messaging_socket_path` of `system/init` are removed. Only `initialize.jsonl` keeps the initialize reply.

- `initialize.jsonl`: an `initialize` control request, then "Reply with the single word: ok". The `control_response` lists `commands` (`name`, `description`, `argumentHint`, and `builtin`, `aliases` on some); the project skill `greet` is first. `system/init` lists the same names under `slash_commands` and the skills under `skills`.
- `question.jsonl`: "Use the AskUserQuestion tool to ask me which colour I like, options red and blue." The `can_use_tool` request for `AskUserQuestion` was answered with `allow` and `updatedInput` set to the questions plus `"answers":{"Which colour do you like?":"red"}`; the tool result and the reply ("You picked red.") show Claude read it.
- `queued.jsonl`: `--permission-mode bypassPermissions --replay-user-messages`. A user line with uuid `1111…` asks for three slow Bash steps; 2 s in, a user line with uuid `2222…` says "Also end your final reply with the word BANANA." It joins the running turn after the first tool result: a `user` line with `isReplay: true` and uuid `2222…` marks the moment, `command_lifecycle` frames mark `queued`, `started` and `completed`, and the one `result` ends with BANANA.
- `fork.jsonl`: `--resume <session> --fork-session --resume-session-at <uuid>`, where the session had two turns ("My first message is the word APPLE." and "My second message is the word ZEBRA.") and the uuid is turn 1's assistant line. Asked for both words, Claude answers `first=APPLE second=NONE`, and `system/init` has a new session id.
- `mode.jsonl`: `--permission-mode plan --replay-user-messages`. A `set_permission_mode` request `mode-1` to `default` is answered with `{"mode":"default"}` and followed by a `system/status` line whose `permissionMode` is `default`; the Write of "Create a file named made.txt with the word ok." then asks with `can_use_tool` (its `permission_suggestions` offer `setMode acceptEdits`). `mode-2` back to `plan` gets the same reply and status line. `mode-3` to `bypassPermissions` on a Claude not started with `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` gets a `control_response` of subtype `error` with `error_code` `bypass_not_launched`.
- `planexit.jsonl`: `--permission-mode plan --replay-user-messages`. "Plan how to add a file named made.txt, then exit plan mode." Claude writes its plan file and asks `can_use_tool` for `ExitPlanMode`; the request was answered with `allow`, after which a `system/status` line reports `permissionMode` `default`. The file Claude then writes asks with `can_use_tool` too. The first turn ran on Sonnet, since plan mode picks the model. Streamed `input_json_delta` events are removed, since they split a path in pieces; the home folder in the plan file's path is replaced with `/tmp/rec`.
- `compact.jsonl`: what Claude writes after a `/compact` user message, written by hand, as the check that ran `/compact` live did not keep its stdout. A `system` line of subtype `compact_boundary` (with `compact_metadata`: `trigger` and `pre_tokens`) marks where the conversation was cut; then `system/init` and the `result`, which are what that check's chat log shows. A later `--resume-session-at` cannot find a message from before the boundary.
- `mcp.jsonl`: `--permission-mode default --replay-user-messages --mcp-config` with a throwaway stdio server named `agentos` that has the tools `echo` (`readOnlyHint`), `poke` and `slow`. `system/init` lists the server in `mcp_servers` (`{"name":"agentos","status":"connected","source":"dynamic"}`) and its tools as `mcp__agentos__echo`, `mcp__agentos__poke`, `mcp__agentos__slow`. "Call the echo tool with the text hi." runs `ToolSearch` first (haiku loads a deferred tool that way), then a `tool_use` named `mcp__agentos__echo` with input `{"text":"hi"}` and a `tool_result` of `echo: hi`. A second user message, "Now call the poke tool.", gets a `tool_result` with `is_error: true` and the content `poke failed: nothing to poke`, which Claude reports. Both calls asked with `can_use_tool` (no `--allowedTools`) and were answered with `allow`.
- `thinking.jsonl`: `--effort high --thinking-display summarized`, with a `notes.txt` in the repo. "Read notes.txt, then tell me in one short sentence why the launch moved. Think about it first." Each of the two API messages starts with a thinking block: a `content_block_start` of type `thinking`, `thinking_delta` events with its text (each followed by a `system/thinking_tokens` line), a `signature_delta`, then the `assistant` line with the whole `thinking` block before its `content_block_stop`. The first message goes on to a `Read` of `notes.txt`, the second to the reply. Without `--thinking-display summarized` Claude 2.1.332 in `-p` sends the same blocks with empty `thinking` text. Streamed `input_json_delta` events are removed, as in `planexit.jsonl`, and so is the `rate_limit_event` line.
- `subagents.jsonl`: `--thinking-display summarized --replay-user-messages --permission-mode bypassPermissions`, with no `--permission-prompt-tool`. "Use two subagents in parallel, in one message with two Agent tool calls: one lists the files in this folder, one counts the lines of README.md. Then tell me both answers in one line." The two `Agent` calls (input `description`, `subagent_type` `Explore`, `prompt`) start in the background: a `system/task_started` line each (`tool_use_id`, `is_backgrounded: true`), a `tool_result` at once that says the agent was launched, and the turn's `result`. The subagents' own `assistant` and `user` lines come after it, each with `parent_tool_use_id` set to its `Agent` call and an `agent_id`; no `stream_event` carries one, so a subagent streams no partial message. `system/task_progress` lines report a subagent's tool count; `system/task_notification` ends each (`tool_use_id`, `status` `completed`, `summary` its report, `usage`), and Claude then runs a turn of its own with no user line, whose `result` has an `origin` of kind `task-notification`. Hook lines, `thinking_tokens`, `command_lifecycle`, `rate_limit_event` and `input_json_delta` lines are removed, `system/init` keeps only `cwd`, `session_id`, `tools`, `model` and `permissionMode`, thinking signatures are emptied, and the task output folder is replaced with `/tmp/claude/tasks`.
- `subagents-wait.jsonl`: the same, with each `Agent` call asked for with `run_in_background` false. `task_started` says `is_backgrounded: false`, a `user` line with `parent_tool_use_id` holds each subagent's prompt as a text block, and each `task_notification` comes before the `tool_result` of its call, which holds the report inside a hand-back frame. Trimmed as `subagents.jsonl`.
- `background.jsonl`: `--thinking-display summarized --replay-user-messages --permission-mode bypassPermissions`. "In ONE message make these two tool calls: (1) the Agent tool, description "Wait then report", prompt: "Run the Bash command: sleep 25 && echo agent-done . Then reply with its output."; (2) the Bash tool with run_in_background true and command: sleep 35 && echo shell-done . Then reply only the word started and end your turn." Both calls start in the background: a `system/task_started` line each with `is_backgrounded: true`, `task_type` `local_agent` for the subagent and `local_bash` for the shell. The turn's `result` comes first. The subagent's foreground `sleep` is blocked, so it starts its own background shell (`task_started` with `owned_by_subagent: true` and `parent_task_id` the subagent's `task_id`) and ends. Claude runs a turn of its own for the subagent's `task_notification`. The subagent's shell ends with an `owned_by_subagent` notification that starts no turn of Claude's: the subagent starts again under the same `tool_use_id` (a second `task_started`, a new `run_id`), reads the shell's output and ends again, and Claude runs a turn for that end, then one for the end of its own shell. Each of those three turns' `result` has an `origin` of kind `task-notification`. Trimmed as `subagents.jsonl`, and `command_lifecycle` lines are removed.
- `subagent-approval.jsonl`: `--thinking-display summarized --replay-user-messages --permission-mode default`. "Make exactly one tool call: the Agent tool with description "Write sub file" and prompt: "Use the Write tool to create the file sub.txt in the current folder with the content ok. Then reply done." Then reply only the word started and end your turn." The turn's `result` comes, then the background subagent's `Write` call and its `can_use_tool` request, which has no `parent_tool_use_id` but names the call in `tool_use_id` and the subagent in `agent_id` (its `task_id`). It was answered with `allow` 44 s later; Claude writes the answer back on its stdout as a `control_response`. The subagent writes the file, ends, and Claude runs a turn for its end. Trimmed as `background.jsonl`.
- `interrupt-approval.jsonl`: the same session, then "Use the Write tool to create main2.txt with the content hi." While its `can_use_tool` request waits, an `interrupt` control request: Claude sends a `control_cancel_request` with the request's id, the reply to the interrupt, a rejected `tool_result` for the call and an `error_during_execution` result. Trimmed as `background.jsonl`.
- `interrupt-background.jsonl`: the same session, then a turn that starts one background subagent and ends; right after its `result`, with no turn running, a plain `interrupt` control request. Claude stops the subagent (`task_updated` `killed`, then `task_notification` with `status: stopped`), answers the interrupt and starts no turn for the end; it hands the notification to Claude at the next user turn instead. Trimmed as `background.jsonl`.
- `interrupt-spare.jsonl`: `--thinking-display summarized --replay-user-messages --permission-mode bypassPermissions`, with `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1` in the environment. "First make one tool call: the Agent tool with description "Slow three" … After that call, you yourself run with the Bash tool in the foreground: python3 -c "import time; time.sleep(25); print(8)" and then reply with its output." While Claude's own Bash runs, an `interrupt` with `spare_background_tasks: true`: the foreground shell ends `stopped`, the turn ends with `error_during_execution`, and the background subagent goes on, ends `completed` 27 s later and gets a turn of Claude's. `system/session_state_changed` says `running` at the first message and again at the subagent's end, and `idle` only after that turn's `result`: Claude counts its background subagent as work. Trimmed as `background.jsonl`.
- `hooks.jsonl`: one run with `--replay-user-messages --permission-mode default`, without `--strict-mcp-config`, and a `--settings` whose seven hooks (`SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `Notification`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) each saved their stdin and then slept 0.4 s, so that the stream shows what waits on a hook. The repo has a folder `sub`. In turn: "Run `cd sub && pwd` with Bash, then say done."; "Write hi to a.txt." (the `Write` asks with `can_use_tool` and is allowed); "Ask me which colour I like, in your reply's last sentence."; "Use AskUserQuestion to ask me yes or no." (answered `Yes`); "Use the Task tool to list the files here." (Claude runs an `Explore` subagent in the foreground with the `Agent` tool); "Run `python3 -c "import time; time.sleep(60)"` with Bash, then say done." (allowed, then 6 s later an `interrupt` with `spare_background_tasks`, which ends the turn with `error_during_execution`); then 75 s with no input, and stdin closed. Claude exits with code 1. The initialize reply, the `rate_limit_event` lines and the `input_json_delta` events are removed; `system/init` loses `memory_paths`, `messaging_socket_path` and the account's claude.ai connector (its `mcp_servers` entry and its tools); `result` loses `credential_expires_at`. Where the text or thinking deltas of one block spelled the working folder, they are joined into the block's first delta. The task output folder is replaced with `/tmp/claude`. The `system/hook_started` and `hook_response` lines are there only because a `SessionStart` hook is set.
- `hooks-payloads.jsonl`: the hook payloads of the same run, in the order the hooks started, each as `{"after":N,"before":M,"payload":{…}}`: the hook started after line N of `hooks.jsonl` and ended before line M. The driver and the hook took the times on one clock, to about 50 ms. Claude's config folder is replaced with `/tmp/claude-config`, so `transcript_path` is `/tmp/claude-config/projects/-tmp-rec/<session_id>.jsonl`. No `Notification` hook ran.
